title: Preliminary Evidence of the Effect of (Anti)feminist Discourse on Attitudes Towards Feminism and the Attribution of (Im)morality to Feminists / Evidencia preliminar sobre el efecto del discurso (anti)feminista en la actitud hacia el feminismo y la atribución de (in)moralidad a las feministas
abstract: Within the framework of persuasion literature, this study empirically explores how (anti)feminist discourses influence recipients’ attitudes towards feminism, their attribution of morality and immorality to feminists and their perception of discrimination against men. Furthermore, it evaluates whether the gender of the source and/or the recipient interacts with the type of discourse, considering ambivalent sexism as a covariate. A total of 306 individuals participated. The results indicate that antifeminist discourse generated a less favourable attitude towards feminism, as well as more attributions of immorality and fewer attributions of morality to feminists. No effects were found for the gender of the source or the recipient, nor were there any interaction effects. The findings underscore the importance of discourse in shaping attitudes towards feminism, with important implications for the promotion of gender equality and the containment of antifeminist rhetoric in society.
